source.text: Καὶ εἶδον οὐρανὸν καινὸν καὶ γῆν καινήν· ὁ γὰρ πρῶτος οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ πρώτη γῆ ἀπῆλθαν, καὶ ἡ θάλασσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἔτι.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw a heaven new and an earth new; for the first heaven and the first earth went away, and the sea not is any longer.

en.L: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea is no more.
en.B: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth; the first heaven and the first earth had gone, and the sea was no more.
en.R: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The first heaven and the first earth were gone. There was no more sea.

decisions.choice: a new heaven and a new earth: Isaiah 65-66
decisions.reason: "For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former things shall not be remembered" (Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; compare 2 Peter 3:13). καινὸν means new in kind, renewed, not merely recent.

decisions.choice: no more sea: the end of chaos and threat
decisions.reason: In Revelation the sea is where the beast came from (13:1) and a place of the dead (20:13); in the Old Testament it often stands for the chaotic powers God subdues (Psalm 74:13; Isaiah 27:1). Its absence most likely means that everything hostile and threatening is gone.

source.text: καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καινὴν εἶδον καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡτοιμασμένην ὡς νύμφην κεκοσμημένην τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And the city the holy, Jerusalem new, I saw coming down out of the heaven from the God, having been prepared as a bride having been adorned for the husband of her.

en.L: And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
en.B: And the holy city, the new Jerusalem, I saw descending out of heaven from God, ready like a bride who has adorned herself for her husband.
en.R: I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem. It was coming down out of heaven from God. It was ready, like a bride dressed in beautiful clothes for her husband.

decisions.choice: the holy city, new Jerusalem, as a bride: Isaiah
decisions.reason: Isaiah calls Jerusalem "the holy city" (52:1) and pictures her as a bride adorned with jewels, in whom God delights as a bridegroom over his bride (61:10; 62:1-5). The city is the bride of the Lamb (19:7; 21:9): God's people, in their final home. It comes down from God: it is his gift, not a human achievement (compare Hebrews 11:10; 12:22).

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου λεγούσης· Ἰδοὺ ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ σκηνώσει μετ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ λαοὶ αὐτοῦ ἔσονται, καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ θεὸς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔσται, καὶ ἐξαλείψει πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ ὁ θάνατος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι· οὔτε πένθος οὔτε κραυγὴ οὔτε πόνος οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι.

records.literal_gloss: And I heard a voice great out of the throne saying: Behold the tent of the God with the men, and he will tent with them, and they peoples of him will be, and he himself the God with them will be, \v 4 and he will wipe out every tear out of the eyes of them, and the death not will be any longer, nor mourning nor crying nor pain will be any longer;

en.L: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, "Look, the dwelling of God [is] with {{gender:human beings|men}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will dwell with them, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} peoples, and God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will be with them, \v 4 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death will be no more, nor will mourning or crying or pain be any more.
en.B: Then I heard a loud voice from the throne: "See, God's dwelling is with {{gender:human beings|men}}! He will make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home with them, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} peoples; God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will be with them. \v 4 Every tear {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will wipe from their eyes. Death will be no more, and no more mourning, no crying, no pain.
en.R: I heard a loud voice from the throne. It said, "Now God's home is with people! God will live with them. They will be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, and God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will be with them. \v 4 He will wipe away all their tears. There will be no more death, no more sadness, no more crying, and no more pain.

decisions.choice: God's dwelling with people: the covenant promise fulfilled
decisions.reason: σκηνὴ is a tent, the word for the tabernacle where God lived among Israel. God promised, "I will make my dwelling among you ... and I will be your God, and you shall be my people" (Leviticus 26:11-12; compare Ezekiel 37:27; Zechariah 2:10-11). John 1:14 uses the verb of the Word made flesh. Now the promise is fully kept.

decisions.choice: peoples (plural)
alternatives: an added phrase, "and he will be their God"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads λαοὶ, "peoples": God's people now come from many nations (compare 21:24). Many manuscripts read the singular, "people", as in the Old Testament promise, and some add "and be their God" after "with them". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: no more tears or death: Isaiah 25:8 and 65:19
decisions.reason: "He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces" (Isaiah 25:8); "no more shall be heard in it the sound of weeping and the cry of distress" (Isaiah 65:19; compare 35:10). The promise of 7:17 is fulfilled.

decisions.choice: human beings | men
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

source.text: τὰ πρῶτα ἀπῆλθαν.

records.literal_gloss: the first things went away.

en.L: the first things have passed away."
en.B: The former things have gone."
en.R: The old things are gone forever."

decisions.choice: the first things: the old order with its sorrow
decisions.reason: "The first things" are the old creation and everything that belonged to it, death, grief and pain (21:1; Isaiah 43:18-19; 65:17).

source.text: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ· Ἰδοὺ καινὰ ποιῶ πάντα.

records.literal_gloss: And said the [one] sitting on the throne: Behold new I make all things.

en.L: And the one seated on the throne said, "Look, I am making all things new."
en.B: And the one who sits on the throne said, "See, I am making everything new!"
en.R: The one sitting on the throne said, "Look! I am making everything new!"

decisions.choice: God himself speaks
decisions.reason: For the first time since 1:8, the one seated on the throne speaks directly. "Behold, I am doing a new thing" (Isaiah 43:19; compare 2 Corinthians 5:17).

source.text: καὶ λέγει· Γράψον, ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And he says: Write, because these the words faithful and true are.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Write, for these words are faithful and true."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Write it down, because these words can be trusted, and they are true."
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Write this down, because these words are true and can be trusted."

decisions.choice: he says: most likely God, continuing
decisions.reason: The speaker is most likely still the one on the throne, though an angel may be meant (compare 19:9; 22:6).

decisions.choice: faithful and true words
decisions.reason: "Faithful and true" are titles of Christ (3:14; 19:11). God's words share his character: they can be relied on and will come to pass (22:6).

source.text: καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Γέγοναν.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me: They have happened.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "They have come to pass!
en.B: He said to me, "It is done!
en.R: Then he said to me, "It is finished!

decisions.choice: they have happened: all that was promised is done
decisions.reason: Γέγοναν is plural: all these things have come to pass. At the seventh bowl a voice said, "It is done" (16:17), of judgment; here it is said of the new creation. The speech continues to 21:8.

decisions.choice: he: deity pronoun setting (L); he (B, R, sentence start)
decisions.reason: The speaker is God; at the start of a sentence the pronoun is capitalized either way.

source.text: ἐγὼ τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος.

records.literal_gloss: I the Alpha and the O, the beginning and the end.

en.L: I [am] the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end.
en.B: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end.
en.R: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end of all things.

decisions.choice: the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end
decisions.reason: See 1:8. Here the title is explained as "the beginning and the end": God is the source of all things and their goal. In 22:13 Christ says the same of himself.

source.text: ἐγὼ τῷ διψῶντι δώσω ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς τοῦ ὕδατος τῆς ζωῆς δωρεάν.

records.literal_gloss: I to the [one] thirsting will give out of the spring of the water of the life freely.

en.L: To the one who thirsts I will give from the spring of the water of life freely.
en.B: To anyone who is thirsty I will give water from the spring of life, free of charge.
en.R: I will give water from the spring of life to anyone who is thirsty. It will cost them nothing.

decisions.choice: water of life, freely given: Isaiah 55:1
decisions.reason: "Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and he who has no money, come, buy and eat!" (Isaiah 55:1). Jesus promised living water to the thirsty (John 4:10-14; 7:37-38). δωρεάν means as a gift, without payment (compare 22:17).

source.text: ὁ νικῶν κληρονομήσει ταῦτα, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ θεὸς καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι υἱός.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] overcoming will inherit these things, and I will be to him God and he will be to me son.

en.L: The one who overcomes will inherit these things, and I will be {{gender:that person's|his}} God, and {{gender:that person|he}} will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:child|son}}.
en.B: Whoever overcomes will inherit these things; I will be {{gender:that person's|his}} God, and {{gender:that person|he}} will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:child|son}}.
en.R: Everyone who wins the victory will receive all these things. I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} {{gender:children|sons}}.

decisions.choice: I will be his God and he my son: 2 Samuel 7:14
decisions.reason: God promised David's heir, "I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son" (2 Samuel 7:14). The promise to the king is given to everyone who overcomes, with the covenant words "I will be their God". The last of the promises to the one who overcomes (2:7-3:21) gathers them all: they inherit everything.

decisions.choice: son: a child and heir of God, man or woman
decisions.reason: υἱός is "son", the heir who inherits (compare Galatians 4:7). It applies to every believer, women and men alike.

decisions.choice: that person's | his; that person | he; child | son
decisions.reason: The promise is for every believer (m2), so the pronouns and "son" take the gender setting.

decisions.choice: overcomes (L, B); wins the victory (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:7.

source.text: τοῖς δὲ δειλοῖς καὶ ἀπίστοις καὶ ἐβδελυγμένοις καὶ φονεῦσι καὶ πόρνοις καὶ φαρμάκοις καὶ εἰδωλολάτραις καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ψευδέσιν τὸ μέρος αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ τῇ καιομένῃ πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ, ὅ ἐστιν ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος.

records.literal_gloss: But to the cowardly and unbelieving and having become detestable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all the liars, the part of them in the lake the burning with fire and sulfur, which is the death the second.

en.L: But for the cowardly and unbelieving and detestable and murderers and sexually immoral and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars, their portion [is] in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death."
en.B: But as for the cowardly, the faithless, the vile, the murderers, the sexually immoral, those who practice sorcery, the idolaters, and all liars, their share is in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. This is the second death."
en.R: But some people are cowards. Some do not believe. Some do disgusting things. Some murder, some commit sexual sins, some use magic, some worship idols, and some lie. Their place will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. That is the second death."

decisions.choice: the cowardly and unbelieving: those who would not stay faithful
decisions.reason: The list begins with the opposite of the one who overcomes: those who out of fear denied Christ, and those who would not believe or be faithful (compare 2:10, 13). The rest of the list names sins condemned throughout the book (9:21; 22:15).

decisions.choice: the second death
decisions.reason: See 20:14-15. On how Christians have understood the lake of fire, see the note on 14:10.

decisions.choice: short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long list into short sentences.

source.text: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας, τῶν γεμόντων τῶν ἑπτὰ πληγῶν τῶν ἐσχάτων, καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετ’ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι τὴν νύμφην τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀρνίου.

records.literal_gloss: And came one of the seven angels the having the seven bowls the being full of the seven plagues the last, and spoke with me saying: Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.

en.L: And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues came and spoke with me, saying, "Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb."
en.B: One of the seven angels, those who had held the seven bowls brimming with the seven last plagues, came and talked with me. "Come," he said, "I will show you the bride, the Lamb's wife."
en.R: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the last seven plagues came to me. He said, "Come, I will show you the bride, the Lamb's wife."

decisions.choice: the same angel's guide as for the prostitute
decisions.reason: The words echo 17:1, where one of the same angels said, "Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute." The two cities are set side by side: the prostitute Babylon and the bride, the new Jerusalem.

source.text: καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με ἐν πνεύματι ἐπὶ ὄρος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν, καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἔχουσαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ· ὁ φωστὴρ αὐτῆς ὅμοιος λίθῳ τιμιωτάτῳ, ὡς λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι κρυσταλλίζοντι·

records.literal_gloss: And he carried away me in spirit onto a mountain great and high, and showed me the city the holy Jerusalem coming down out of the heaven from the God, \v 11 having the glory of the God; the radiance of it like to a stone most precious, as to a stone jasper being clear as crystal.

en.L: And he carried me away in [the] Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God, \v 11 having the glory of God; its radiance [was] like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal.
en.B: He took me away in the Spirit to a mountain, vast and high, and showed me Jerusalem, the holy city, descending out of heaven from God, \v 11 radiant with the glory of God. It shone like the costliest of stones, like jasper, clear as crystal.
en.R: Then the Spirit took hold of me, and the angel carried me to a very high mountain. He showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God. \v 11 It was full of God's glory. It sparkled like a very valuable jewel, like a jasper stone, as clear as crystal.

decisions.choice: a high mountain: Ezekiel 40:2
decisions.reason: "In visions of God he brought me ... and set me down on a very high mountain, on which was a structure like a city" (Ezekiel 40:2). To see the prostitute John was taken to a wilderness (17:3); to see the bride, to a mountain.

decisions.choice: the glory of God: his presence fills the city
decisions.reason: The city shines with God's own glory, the brightness that once filled the tabernacle and temple (Exodus 40:34; Isaiah 60:1-2). Jasper is the stone that described God in 4:3.

decisions.choice: the Spirit took hold of me (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:10.

source.text: ἔχουσα τεῖχος μέγα καὶ ὑψηλόν, ἔχουσα πυλῶνας δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν ἀγγέλους δώδεκα, καὶ ὀνόματα ἐπιγεγραμμένα ἅ ἐστιν τῶν δώδεκα φυλῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ·

records.literal_gloss: having a wall great and high, having gates twelve, and at the gates angels twelve, and names having been inscribed, which are of the twelve tribes of sons of Israel.

en.L: having a great and high wall, having twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed, which are [the names] of the twelve tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: Around it ran a wall, great and high, with twelve gates. Twelve angels stood at the gates, and names were inscribed on them, the names of the twelve tribes of the Israelites.
en.R: The city had a high, thick wall with twelve gates. There was an angel at each gate. The names of the twelve tribes of Israel were written on the gates.

decisions.choice: twelve gates named for the tribes: Ezekiel 48
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's city has twelve gates, three on each side, named after the twelve tribes of Israel (Ezekiel 48:30-35). The angels guard the gates. Israel's story is built into the city.

decisions.choice: children of Israel (L); the Israelites (B); Israel (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:14.

source.text: ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ βορρᾶ πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ νότου πυλῶνες τρεῖς, καὶ ἀπὸ δυσμῶν πυλῶνες τρεῖς·

records.literal_gloss: From east gates three, and from north gates three, and from south gates three, and from west gates three.

en.L: On the east three gates, and on the north three gates, and on the south three gates, and on the west three gates.
en.B: Three gates faced east, three north, three south, and three west.
en.R: There were three gates on each side of the city: east, north, south, and west.

decisions.choice: gates on every side: open to all directions
decisions.reason: The city faces every direction of the earth. Its gates are never shut (21:25), and the nations walk by its light (21:24).

source.text: καὶ τὸ τεῖχος τῆς πόλεως ἔχων θεμελίους δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα ὀνόματα τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τοῦ ἀρνίου.

records.literal_gloss: And the wall of the city having foundations twelve, and on them twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

en.L: And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
en.B: Twelve foundation stones held up the city's wall, and on them were the twelve names of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
en.R: The wall of the city was built on twelve foundation stones. The names of the Lamb's twelve apostles were written on them.

decisions.choice: the tribes and the apostles: one people of God
decisions.reason: The gates bear the names of Israel's tribes and the foundations the names of the apostles. Ephesians 2:20 speaks of the church as built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets. The people of God of both covenants form one city (compare the twenty-four elders, 4:4).

source.text: Καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἶχεν μέτρον κάλαμον χρυσοῦν, ἵνα μετρήσῃ τὴν πόλιν καὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας αὐτῆς καὶ τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] speaking with me had a measure reed golden, so that he might measure the city and the gates of it and the wall of it.

en.L: And the one speaking with me had a measure, a golden reed, so that he might measure the city and its gates and its wall.
en.B: The one speaking with me held a golden reed for measuring, to take the measurements of the city, its gates, and its wall.
en.R: The angel who was talking with me had a gold measuring stick. He used it to measure the city, its gates, and its wall.

decisions.choice: measuring the city: Ezekiel 40
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel's vision a man with a measuring reed measures the temple (Ezekiel 40:3-5); in 11:1 John measured the temple. Measuring shows that the city is God's, ordered and secure.

source.text: καὶ ἡ πόλις τετράγωνος κεῖται, καὶ τὸ μῆκος αὐτῆς ὅσον τὸ πλάτος.

records.literal_gloss: And the city foursquare lies, and the length of it as much as the width.

en.L: And the city lies foursquare, and its length [is] as great as [its] width.
en.B: The city is built as a square; its length is the same as its width.
en.R: The city was square. It was as long as it was wide.

decisions.choice: foursquare: a perfect square
decisions.reason: τετράγωνος means having four equal sides. Ezekiel's city is also square (Ezekiel 48:16, 20).

source.text: καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὴν πόλιν τῷ καλάμῳ ἐπὶ σταδίους δώδεκα χιλιάδων· τὸ μῆκος καὶ τὸ πλάτος καὶ τὸ ὕψος αὐτῆς ἴσα ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: And he measured the city with the reed at stadia twelve thousands; the length and the width and the height of it equal are.

en.L: And he measured the city with the reed: 12,000 stadia; its length and width and height are equal.
en.B: He measured the city with the reed: {{units:about 1,400 miles|12,000 stadia}}. Its length, its width, and its height are the same.
en.R: He measured the city with the measuring stick. It was {{units:about 1,400 miles|12,000 stadia}} long. It was just as wide and just as high.

decisions.choice: a cube: the city is the holy of holies
decisions.reason: The inner room of Solomon's temple, the most holy place, was a cube (1 Kings 6:20). The whole city is shaped like it: all of it is the place of God's presence (21:22).

decisions.choice: 12,000 stadia: immense, and a number of God's people
decisions.reason: A stadion was about 600 feet, so 12,000 stadia is about 1,400 miles, larger than any city imaginable. Twelve thousand is twelve times a thousand, the number of God's people (7:4-8). Whether it gives the length of each side or the whole circuit is not said.

decisions.choice: units: about 1,400 miles | 12,000 stadia
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek measure; Balanced and Readable give a modern equivalent with the original as the alternative.

source.text: καὶ ἐμέτρησεν τὸ τεῖχος αὐτῆς ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τεσσάρων πηχῶν, μέτρον ἀνθρώπου, ὅ ἐστιν ἀγγέλου.

records.literal_gloss: And he measured the wall of it a hundred forty four cubits, a measure of a man, which is of an angel.

en.L: And he measured its wall: 144 cubits, a human measure, which is [also] an angel's.
en.B: He measured its wall too: {{units:about 216 feet|144 cubits}} by human measure, which the angel was using.
en.R: He also measured the wall. It measured {{units:about 216 feet|144 cubits}} by the ordinary human measure, which the angel was using.

decisions.choice: 144 cubits: twelve times twelve
decisions.reason: A cubit is about 18 inches, so 144 cubits is about 216 feet. The text does not say whether this is the wall's height or its thickness. The number is twelve times twelve, like the 144,000 (7:4), and it is small next to the city's size: the wall is a sign of security, not of defense against an enemy.

decisions.choice: a human measure, which is also an angel's
decisions.reason: The angel uses ordinary units of measurement, so John and his readers can understand the figures.

decisions.choice: units: about 216 feet | 144 cubits
decisions.reason: As in 21:16.

source.text: καὶ ἡ ἐνδώμησις τοῦ τείχους αὐτῆς ἴασπις, καὶ ἡ πόλις χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὅμοιον ὑάλῳ καθαρῷ·

records.literal_gloss: And the material of the wall of it jasper, and the city gold pure like to glass pure.

en.L: And the material of its wall [was] jasper, and the city pure gold, like clear glass.
en.B: The wall was made of jasper, and the city itself was pure gold, clear like glass.
en.R: The wall was made of jasper. The city was made of pure gold, as clear as glass.

decisions.choice: pure gold like clear glass: a city full of light
decisions.reason: The inner room of the temple was overlaid with pure gold (1 Kings 6:20-22). This gold is clear as glass: God's light passes through the whole city (21:23).

source.text: οἱ θεμέλιοι τοῦ τείχους τῆς πόλεως παντὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ κεκοσμημένοι· ὁ θεμέλιος ὁ πρῶτος ἴασπις, ὁ δεύτερος σάπφιρος, ὁ τρίτος χαλκηδών, ὁ τέταρτος σμάραγδος, ὁ πέμπτος σαρδόνυξ, ὁ ἕκτος σάρδιον, ὁ ἕβδομος χρυσόλιθος, ὁ ὄγδοος βήρυλλος, ὁ ἔνατος τοπάζιον, ὁ δέκατος χρυσόπρασος, ὁ ἑνδέκατος ὑάκινθος, ὁ δωδέκατος ἀμέθυστος·

records.literal_gloss: The foundations of the wall of the city with every stone precious having been adorned; the foundation the first jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, \v 20 the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, the twelfth amethyst.

en.L: The foundations of the wall of the city [were] adorned with every precious stone: the first foundation jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, \v 20 the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, the twelfth amethyst.
en.B: Every kind of precious stone adorned the foundations of the city wall: the first was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, \v 20 the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst.
en.R: The foundation stones of the city wall were decorated with all kinds of jewels. The first was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, \v 20 the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst.

decisions.choice: twelve jewels: the high priest's breastpiece and Isaiah's city
decisions.reason: The high priest wore a breastpiece set with twelve stones, one for each tribe (Exodus 28:17-21), and many of the same stones appear here. Isaiah promised Jerusalem foundations of sapphires and walls of precious stones (Isaiah 54:11-12). The whole people of God is now the priestly city.

decisions.choice: the names of the stones
decisions.reason: Ancient names of stones do not always match the stones that bear those names today, so the exact colors are uncertain.

decisions.choice: traditional names of the stones
decisions.reason: Every level uses the traditional English forms of the Greek names, since their modern identification is uncertain (m2).

source.text: καὶ οἱ δώδεκα πυλῶνες δώδεκα μαργαρῖται, ἀνὰ εἷς ἕκαστος τῶν πυλώνων ἦν ἐξ ἑνὸς μαργαρίτου· καὶ ἡ πλατεῖα τῆς πόλεως χρυσίον καθαρὸν ὡς ὕαλος διαυγής.

records.literal_gloss: And the twelve gates twelve pearls, each one of the gates was out of one pearl. And the street of the city gold pure as glass transparent.

en.L: And the twelve gates [were] twelve pearls; each one of the gates was of a single pearl. And the street of the city [was] pure gold, like transparent glass.
en.B: Each of the twelve gates was a pearl: every gate was cut from one single pearl. And the city's broad street was of pure gold, transparent as glass.
en.R: Each of the twelve gates was made from one huge pearl. The main street of the city was made of pure gold, as clear as glass.

decisions.choice: pearl gates and a golden street: beyond any earthly wealth
decisions.reason: Pearls were among the most valuable things in the ancient world (Matthew 13:45-46), and Babylon traded in them (18:12). Here a single pearl forms a whole gate. πλατεῖα is the city's broad street or square; it may mean its streets in general.

source.text: Καὶ ναὸν οὐκ εἶδον ἐν αὐτῇ, ὁ γὰρ κύριος, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ναὸς αὐτῆς ἐστιν, καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον.

records.literal_gloss: And temple not I saw in it, for the Lord the God the Almighty temple of it is, and the Lamb.

en.L: And I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God the Almighty is its temple, and the Lamb.
en.B: There was no temple to be seen in the city: its temple is the Lord God, the Almighty, and the Lamb.
en.R: There was no temple in the city. The Lord God, the Almighty, and the Lamb are its temple.

decisions.choice: no temple: God's presence fills everything
decisions.reason: A temple marked off a holy place where God was present. In the new Jerusalem there is no such boundary: God and the Lamb are present everywhere, and the whole city is the holy of holies (21:16).

source.text: καὶ ἡ πόλις οὐ χρείαν ἔχει τοῦ ἡλίου οὐδὲ τῆς σελήνης, ἵνα φαίνωσιν αὐτῇ, ἡ γὰρ δόξα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐφώτισεν αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ λύχνος αὐτῆς τὸ ἀρνίον.

records.literal_gloss: And the city no need has of the sun nor of the moon, that they shine in it, for the glory of the God lit it, and the lamp of it the Lamb.

en.L: And the city has no need of the sun or of the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gave it light, and its lamp [is] the Lamb.
en.B: Neither sun nor moon is needed to give the city light; God's glory lights it up, and its lamp is the Lamb.
en.R: The city does not need the sun or the moon to give it light. God's glory shines on it, and the Lamb is its light.

decisions.choice: no sun or moon: Isaiah 60:19-20
decisions.reason: "The sun shall be no more your light by day ... but the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory" (Isaiah 60:19-20).

source.text: καὶ περιπατήσουσιν τὰ ἔθνη διὰ τοῦ φωτὸς αὐτῆς· καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς φέρουσιν τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν εἰς αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: And will walk the nations by the light of it, and the kings of the earth bring the glory of them into it.

en.L: And the nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it.
en.B: By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth bring their glory.
en.R: The people of all nations will live in its light. The kings of the earth will bring their glory into the city.

decisions.choice: nations and kings come to the city's light: Isaiah 60
decisions.reason: "Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising ... the wealth of the nations shall come to you" (Isaiah 60:3, 5, 11). The kings of the earth, who once served the beast and mourned Babylon (17:2; 18:9), now bring their glory to God's city. How far this describes the conversion of the nations the text does not say.

source.text: καὶ οἱ πυλῶνες αὐτῆς οὐ μὴ κλεισθῶσιν ἡμέρας, νὺξ γὰρ οὐκ ἔσται ἐκεῖ, καὶ οἴσουσιν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: And the gates of it not not will be shut by day, for night not will be there, \v 26 and they will bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it.

en.L: And its gates will never be shut by day, for there will be no night there, \v 26 and they will bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it.
en.B: Its gates will never be shut in the daytime, and there will be no night there. \v 26 Into it people will bring the glory and the honor of the nations.
en.R: Its gates will never be closed during the day, and there will never be any night there. \v 26 The glory and honor of the nations will be brought into the city.

decisions.choice: gates never shut: Isaiah 60:11
decisions.reason: City gates were shut at night for safety. "Your gates shall be open continually; day and night they shall not be shut" (Isaiah 60:11). In the new city there is no night and no danger, so the gates are always open.

decisions.choice: the glory and honor of the nations
decisions.reason: What is good and honorable in the life of the nations is brought into the city, purified (21:27). οἴσουσιν "they will bring" has no named subject; it continues 21:24.

source.text: καὶ οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτὴν πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ποιῶν βδέλυγμα καὶ ψεῦδος, εἰ μὴ οἱ γεγραμμένοι ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου.

records.literal_gloss: And not not will enter into it anything common and the [one] doing abomination and lie, except those having been written in the book of the life of the Lamb.

en.L: And nothing unclean will ever enter into it, nor anyone who does what is detestable and false, except those who are written in the Lamb's book of life.
en.B: Nothing unclean will ever come into it, no one who practices what is detestable or lives a lie; only those written in the Lamb's book of life will enter.
en.R: Nothing that is unclean will ever enter the city. No one who does disgusting things or tells lies will go in. Only the people whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will enter.

decisions.choice: nothing unclean will enter: Isaiah 52:1
decisions.reason: "There shall no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean" (Isaiah 52:1). κοινὸν means common or ritually unclean, unfit for God's presence.

decisions.choice: the Lamb's book of life
decisions.reason: See 3:5; 13:8; 20:15. Those who enter are those the Lamb has written in his book.
